target.title: fix(telemetry): record session.ended trajectory event after flush, not inline with model.completed
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102014 — the `session.ended` trajectory event timestamp equals the last
`model.completed` timestamp, making it impossible to measure actual session
duration vs model compute time.

## Root Cause

`session.ended` was recorded inside the try block immediately after
`model.completed` in the same synchronous execution. Both events called
`new Date().toISOString()` within the same millisecond, producing identical
timestamps. The event was recorded before `flushEmbeddedAttemptTrajectoryRecorder`
and all session cleanup, so the timestamp did not reflect the actual session
end time.

## Fix

Defer `session.ended` to after the trajectory recorder flush in the finally
block. The event is now recorded only when the session actually ends, after
cleanup is complete. The `terminalError` field is captured while still in
scope and forwarded to the finally block.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

Trajectory export from a live agent session on this branch:

```
session.started     ts=2026-07-08T06:32:15.759Z  seq=1
model.completed     ts=2026-07-08T06:32:22.698Z  seq=5
session.ended       ts=2026-07-08T06:32:22.717Z  seq=7
```

`session.ended` (22.717) is 19ms after `model.completed` (22.698), with
different sequence numbers, proving the event is now recorded independently
after the flush instead of in the same synchronous block.

Before the fix, both events shared the same millisecond timestamp because
they were recorded inline. Now the order is: model.completed → flush →
session.ended.

### Autoreview (claude-sonnet-5)

```
autoreview --mode branch --engine claude --model claude-sonnet-5
→ patch is correct (0.95), no accepted/actionable findings
```

- [x] `oxfmt --check` passes
- [x] `oxlint` passes
- [x] `git diff --check` passes
- [x] autoreview clean (claude-sonnet-5, 0.95)
